sources.entry: far2l - Linux/Mac fork of FAR Manager v2

summary.one_liner: far2l is a Linux (also macOS and BSD) port of the FAR Manager v2 file manager, a text-mode dual-panel file manager with many plugins.
summary.what_it_does: far2l is a fork of FAR Manager v2 for Linux, also said to work on macOS and BSD (BSD not regularly tested). It runs in several UI backends: a plain terminal (TTY) mode, TTY modes that use X11 for clipboard and keyboard, and GUI modes built on wxWidgets or SDL. The README lists a large set of plugins, including NetRocks for SFTP/SCP/FTP/FTPS/SMB/NFS/WebDAV/AWS S3, multiarc and arclite for archives, hexitor for hex editing, colorer for syntax highlighting, ImageViewer, MTP and ADB access, a Python scripting plugin, and Transformer for external-command text transformations. Keyboard shortcuts follow the Windows FAR Manager tradition. The README also documents clipboard access via OSC 52 and a set of terminals and SSH clients with extended keyboard support. Build options are set through CMake flags that enable or disable individual plugins and optional dependencies.
use_cases: browse and manage files in a terminal on a Linux or macOS server
transfer files to remote servers over SFTP, FTP, SMB or S3 from a dual-panel manager
edit text and hex files with editor plugins
view images from a file manager
manage Android devices via ADB or MTP
run a FAR-style file manager on a desktop with a GUI backend
how_to_run: Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install far2l-wx (GUI|WX) or sudo apt install far2l (TTY X/Xi) or sudo apt install --no-install-recommends far2l (plain TTY)
macOS/Linux via Homebrew: brew install far2l-tty (compact TTY-only version)
Build from source: git clone the repo, mkdir -p _build && cd _build
Run from ./install/far2l or install with sudo cmake --install .
Docker: docker build . -t far2l && docker run -it far2l
notable: Multiple UI backends (plain TTY, TTY|X, TTY|Xi, GUI|WX, GUI|SDL) that automatically fall back when components are missing
NetRocks plugin covers SFTP, SCP, FTP, FTPS, SMB, NFS, WebDAV and AWS S3 in one panel
Sticky-key and OSC 52 clipboard workarounds for keys that desktop environments usually capture
Many FAR-style plugins with per-plugin CMake flags to turn them off
Packaged in Debian/Ubuntu, Homebrew, PPA, and Docker, with a Nix packaging option
caveats: README labels the project a BETA version and says to use it at your own risk
BSD support is not regularly tested; macOS GUI via Homebrew cask is deprecated because of Apple signing requirements
Some keyboard shortcuts need global desktop shortcut release or workarounds, and clipboard in plain TTY depends on terminal OSC 52 support
Homebrew compact TTY build lacks Python plugins and SMB support; the full build comes from a third-party tap
Only English, Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian translations are considered valid
